adelheid.title: Poison Taster
adelheid.text:
Adelheid has decided that your food must be tasted for poison. She means all of it, at every meal.

She arrives at your table with her own silver spoon. She tries the tavern stew and waits a full minute with her eyes narrowed. She breaks the bread and smells it. She turns one pear over in her gauntlet for so long, as though an assassin might be hiding under the skin, that the cook comes out to ask if something is wrong with it.

You point out that nobody in Hollowmere wants you dead. You owe most of them money.

"That is precisely the motive I would expect," she says.

She tastes the last bite and pronounces it safe. Then she doesn't leave. She stands at your shoulder long after the plate is clean.

"I should say," she begins stiffly, with her eyes on the wall, "that of all my watches, this hour has become the one I look forward to."
ngpp: Mid-bite she pauses, staring down at the spiced stew. She mutters that she somehow knows you dislike fennel. She sets the spoon down. She cannot tell where she learned it, and it bothers her.
"Forgive an old soldier's odd instinct, Sam," she says stiffly, pushing the sweet pear toward your preferred side before tasting it. "I do not know why I know that. I find I do know it."

Adelheid skips the inspection tonight and shares the plate beside your elbow. "I cannot recall why I trust your table above any fortress kitchen, Sam. I only know that I do. I have trusted it before."

choices.label: Ask her to stay for the whole meal
choices.res: She sits across from you in her armor, straight-backed, and eats a whole meal as a guest instead of a guard for the first time. She is very bad at it. She holds the spoon like a dagger. She reports on the stew between bites, as if for the record. By the pear she has stopped checking the doors, and her shoulders have dropped an inch.

choices.label: Tell her she's allowed to finish the pear
choices.res: "Strictly for safety," you say, and hand her the pear. {N} accepts it as a sacred duty. She eats it in tiny, reverent bites, with her eyes closed for the first of them, and juice on her chin she doesn't notice. When she's finished she looks at the core with some regret and writes nothing in her log. You decide not to mention it.

image.comp: in armor tasting food from his plate with great seriousness, napkin tucked in
image.setting: inn dining room at dinner time

adelheid.title: Rain Barrel
adelheid.text:
You cut through the training yard on your way to the cellar, and Adelheid is at the rain barrel.

She's been at sword practice since before dawn. The half-plate is stacked neatly on the bench. She is washing with a bucket and a cloth, and cold water is streaming down her scarred shoulders and her short platinum hair is plastered flat to her head. She has a towel held against her front with one hand.

She sees you, and six years of drill take over.

She snaps to attention and salutes. She does it with the hand that was holding the towel.

There's a moment in which the towel, no longer held as well as it should be, considers its options. Adelheid's face goes from white to scarlet. She does not lower the salute, because you haven't returned it.

1.title: Out of Armor
1.text:
You step into the washroom after the evening watch. Adelheid is already there, wrapped in a thick linen towel, with her short platinum hair wet against her neck. She's working oil into a fresh bruise on her shoulder and not reaching it very well.

She sees it's you. She doesn't snap upright, and she doesn't bolt. She swallows once. Her ears are scarlet, and her steel-blue eyes have gone soft.

"Ah. I thought you were already asleep, Sam." She looks at the vial in her hand and then back at you. "I can't reach the back of it. I wouldn't ordinarily ask. I find I would like to ask you."

choices.label: Take the salve jar and rub her scarred shoulders gently
choices.res: You take the jar and rub her scarred shoulders. Adelheid closes her eyes tightly as your knuckles press through knotted sword muscle. She sits stiff as a lance for three seconds, and then the whole line of her back gives. She leans into your palms and breathes out. When you stop, she turns her face up for a slow, trembling kiss.
choices.fallbackRes: She sits stiff as a lance for three seconds. Then she lets out a long breath, and the knight goes out of her, and she leans her damp head back against your wrist. You work the bruise gently, with the oil on your thumbs. She says nothing at all. She doesn't ask you to stop, and when you do she stays where she is.

choices.label: Leave a warm cup of cider on the stool and step back
choices.res: You set a warm cup of cider on the stool, look at the wall and step back. "Thank you, Sam," she says, quietly and with some surprise. She picks it up in both hands and drinks. Her quiet smile follows you out into the hall, and you hear her put the vial down and not pick it up again for a long time.

3.title: Unarmored
3.text:
The washroom is full of steam from wall to wall, and for once there isn't a scrap of steel anywhere near Adelheid. Her sword belt is hanging on the peg by the door. Her armor is somewhere else entirely.

She's sitting in the cedar tub with the water lapping at her collarbones, naked, her old scars pale against skin flushed pink by the heat. She doesn't cover her tits or look away. She meets your eyes and holds out one wet hand.

"Bolt the door, Sam. My duty ended an hour ago." A very small smile. "I am told that a knight is permitted to want things, off watch. I want you in here with me."

choices.label: Slide into the hot tub and hold her close
choices.res: You slide into the hot water and hold out your arms. All the knightly stiffness melts at once. Adelheid climbs across your thighs, her scarred shoulders streaming, and bites down on her lip as she settles against you. Her hands grip your neck. "I have wanted to do this," she says, in her formal voice, and kisses you with her whole careful self.

choices.label: Kneel beside the tub and take care of her slowly
choices.res: You kneel beside the tub and take her hand off the rim. Her knuckles are white from the oak. You take her wet knees in your palms, and the hot water breaks against your sleeves. "Sam," she says, once, in the voice of a woman giving an order and discovering she cannot. She yields to you completely, with her head back and her eyes shut.

choices.label: Turn around immediately
choices.res: You turn around at once. "Thank you, Sir Sam," she says, in a very small voice, after your footsteps retreat. She holds the towel with both hands for the rest of the day, and for the rest of the week she checks the yard before she washes. But she salutes you at dinner, and it is not quite the same salute.

choices.label: Salute back
choices.res: You salute back. For a moment she is silent. Then she laughs. It's a real, startled laugh, the first you have ever heard from her, rough and surprised, like a door that hasn't been opened in years. She is holding the towel in both hands by then. She laughs until she has to sit down on the bench, scarlet and delighted, and cannot stop.

choices.label: Stammer helplessly
choices.res: You stammer. She stammers back. You stand there in the yard, two grown adults saying nothing in the wrong order, until a goose interrupts, honking, and the knight loses her last thread of dignity. She starts laughing and presses her free hand over her mouth. You are both still standing there when the goose wins.

image.comp: snapping to attention beside a rain barrel, soaking wet, covering herself with one arm and saluting with the other
image.setting: training yard behind an inn, afternoon

adelheid.title: Knight and Her Lord
adelheid.text:
You're looking for the spare lamp oil in the tack room when you knock Adelheid's saddlebag off its hook.

Books fall out. There are nine of them, with cracked spines and embossed covers. Flowers have been pressed between the pages, and every one has a ribbon marking a chapter. You pick one up. It's called The Lady's Sworn Sword. So, more or less, are the rest. Every one of them is about a knight and the lord she serves.

The door bangs open. Adelheid has her sword half out of the scabbard before she sees what you're holding. Then she draws it the rest of the way.

"Put that down. That is private correspondence. You will forget what you have seen." Her face is scarlet to the roots of her hair, and the point of the blade is shaking.

Nobody moves. Then she lowers the sword an inch.

"Have you," she asks, very quietly, "read the third one?"

choices.label: Show her how volume three actually ends
choices.res: She lowers the blade three inches, then drops it, along with the dog-eared novel, onto the floor. She lets you pull her down beside the barracks lamp. Scarlet from jaw to collar, she tells you the third volume was very unrealistic. You tell her you'd like to find out. She takes your face in both hands, and the fiction turns real.

choices.label: Ask which part of the third one is her favorite
choices.res: She tells you, with the sword still half drawn and her eyes fixed on a point past your shoulder. It is the chapter in the rain. She describes it in detail, mostly to the wall, in the voice she uses to read orders. You take careful notes, as is tradition, and she lets you. When she's done she sheathes the blade without looking at it.

choices.label: Hand the books back and promise silence
choices.res: You swear silence on your honor, which causes her to blush deeper. {N} sheathes the sword with great ceremony, takes the books back one at a time, and puts each in her saddlebag. At the last one she hesitates. "Would you," she says, "care to borrow volume two?" She holds it out at arm's length, like a cut flower.

image.comp: pointing a sword at him while clutching a stack of romance novels to her chest, scarlet

adelheid.title: The Report
adelheid.text:
The Radiant Order has sent Adelheid a letter with three seals on it. They require a full report on the hero she is sworn to. In particular they want an account of "the sinful nature of his enterprise".

She has been at the desk for three hours. The page in front of her is blank. The candle has burned down to a stub and the quill is chewed ragged at the end.

If she writes what the Order expects, she will be lying about the women here, whom she has come to respect. If she writes what's true, they will recall her, or do something worse.

Her oath and her honesty have never pulled in different directions before. She doesn't know what to do with her hands, so one of them is tapping her sword hilt against the edge of the desk, over and over.

She looks up when you come in. "I do not know how to describe you to them," she says. "I've tried. I keep describing a good man."
ngpp: She lifts the quill, then stops. She frowns, as if she has already defended this ledger and this house before an inquisitor, in a dream she can't place. The ink dries on the nib.
"Strangely, I know how every line of this defense ends before I write it, Sam," she mutters, gripping the parchment. "I have done this before. I am almost sure. I lost nothing. I think I won."
Adelheid signs her name down the page without hesitation. "No tribunal erases what my heart knows of this house, Sam. I have written this letter in other lives. Let them read the truth again."

choices.label: "Tell them the truth."
choices.res: "Tell them the truth." She writes three pages. Fair wages, rest days, no one here against her will. She reads them twice and seals them with pride, the wax pressed hard. The Order's courier takes them at dawn. She stands at the gate until he's out of sight, then comes back and sits beside you, close, and doesn't say anything.

choices.label: "Could you... leave some things out?"
choices.res: "I will not lie, Sam Takahashi." Her face goes hard, and the quill snaps in her fingers. "Not even for you. I would have thought you knew that." It is a long, cold week. She guards your door like a stranger, and speaks to you only in reports. You catch her watching you once, and she turns the page.

choices.label: Go to the Order with her
choices.res: You go to the Order with her. You answer their questions yourself, politely, for four hours, about wages and rest days and the girls. Adelheid stands beside you the entire time, shoulders squared, not once looking away. When it is over, outside in the rain, she takes your sleeve and holds it a long moment, saying nothing.

image.comp: sitting at a desk staring at a blank page, quill frozen, troubled expression

adelheid.title: Swordplay
adelheid.text:
Adelheid decides that a house owner can't rely on locks and good manners alone. She fetches you out into the yard at dawn, with frost still on the cobbles, and puts a weighted ashwood practice sword in your hands.

It's heavier than it looks. By the fifth parry your wrists are howling. By the tenth, a rooster has come out onto the coop roof to heckle.

She's a good teacher, which surprises you. She doesn't shout. She walks around you, moves your elbow two inches with one finger, and steps back to look. The first sun catches her hair.

"Feet wider, Sam. Guard high. Again."

You do it again. You're terrible. She nods as if you weren't.

"I will not always be at your door," she says, adjusting your grip. "I intend to be. But I've read enough accounts to know how they tend to go. I would sleep better if you could hold a blade for one minute. Again."

2.text:
Adelheid has you out in the frosty yard at dawn again with two ashwood practice blades. She stands closer than any sergeant would. When she corrects the height of your elbow, her bare fingers stay on your forearm afterward.

"Feet wider, Sam. Guard high."

Her voice is as level as ever. But every time you step inside her reach, her eyes drop to your mouth for a moment before she remembers the lesson. She's left her gauntlets on the bench this morning, and her collar is unlaced.

On the next pass she lets you get much nearer than she should. You suspect that a knight of her skill doesn't make that mistake by accident.

image.comp: demonstrating sword guard posture in a misty morning courtyard, correcting the man's grip on a wooden practice blade
image.setting: dawn inn courtyard with wooden fence and training post

choices.label: Practice until you drop
choices.res: You practice until you drop. You drop twice, and once into the water trough. She tries to look stern, fails, and lets her warm hand linger on your shoulder long past helping you up. By midday the rooster has fallen silent and your wrists have stopped hurting in the way that means something. "Again," she says, but she says it softly.

choices.label: Let her win on purpose
choices.res: You let her win on purpose. She knows, and she hates that. Her scar-split brow lowers dangerously. She stops the bout, sets her blade point down on the cobbles and says, quietly, that she does not need to be handled. "Again, and properly this time." You do it properly, and lose, and she is visibly pleased.

choices.label: Disarm her and collect a reward back inside
choices.res: On the seventh exchange you catch her blade, step inside her reach, and hold it there. Adelheid goes still. A flush climbs her neck. Then she drops her sword on the frosty cobbles and walks with you, smiling, back through the warm side door. "A reward," she says, in her formal voice, "is not forbidden." She locks it behind you.

adelheid.title: The Amended Oath
adelheid.text:
Adelheid asks you to come with her to the chapel hall after the house has closed. It's empty at this hour. A few candles are burning, and they turn her short hair to silver.

She kneels, lays her sword across her palms, and renews her oath to you, as she does every month. Sword and life, to the one who was promised. You've stopped trying to talk her out of it.

When she has finished, she stays on her knees.

"My oath was to guard you," she says. "I swore it before I had met you, to a hero in a foretelling. I would like to amend it, now that I know who you are." Her voice is steady. Her hand, when she takes yours, is not. "I wish to stand beside you, and not behind your shoulder. I wish to be yours, Sam, and I am asking whether you'll have me."

She rises, and she doesn't let go of your hand.
ngpp: Her voice trembles over the final vow, and it isn't doubt. It is a sudden vertigo, as if she has knelt on these stones for you before, in other candlelight, and does not know how.

"Forgive me," Adelheid whispers, holding your hand fast. "Why does pledging beside you feel like coming home to a vow already sworn?" She looks at the candles, then at you. "I think I have said this."
"Time and memory both bow to what steel remembers, Sam," Adelheid says, and rises into your arms. "I have knelt here before. I have asked this before. Every cycle, my oath belongs to you."
adelheid.goLead: Adelheid unbuckles her sword belt and sets it down beside the chapel candles. Then she steps into your arms and kisses you, shaken and certain, as the latch clicks shut behind you.

choices.label: Say yes
Not yet
choices.res: {N} bows her head, stiff with discipline. "I can wait. Don't make it too long." She resumes her post by your door, and stands one pace closer. When you look back down the hall she is still looking at the floor, with the faintest smile on her face.
